analysis:
Both units are unchanged base-side CHANGELOG.md history (lines 3652-4066: v0.9.10-v0.9.17 entries). The file_changes map (range_map_complete=true) shows that the only change is near the top: base 11-13 becomes head 11-39, which replaces the v0.10.9 candidate header with v0.10.10 waitlist notes. The examined lines are historical documentation, so this changelog text adds no runtime behavior and no new attack surface, and none of these lines changed.

The new head text (lines 11-39, outside these units) describes the following:
- `darkbloom waitlist`.
- Approval gating for new sandbox setup (TB-013/T-061) and for new cluster pairing (TB-014/T-062).
- Existing setups are never asked.
- 'If the coordinator does not offer waitlists yet, both new setups go on as in 0.10.9'. This is a deliberate fail-open compatibility path.

The approval gating is coordinator-advisory UX. It is not a security control in the canonical model: TB-013 and TB-014 rely on owner confirmation, installer authenticity and the administrator prompt, not on a waitlist. Integration should still confirm two points in the source: that waitlist responses from the coordinator cannot inject commands or paths into the sandbox installer or the gpu-limit flows, and that the 'not offered' fallback cannot be triggered in a way that bypasses those owner and administrator confirmations.

No regression was identified in these units.
